title: Do LLMs exhibit human-like response biases? A case study in survey design

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring changes in LLM response distributions when survey questions are modified to an agree/disagree format to see if models disproportionately agree with the presented statement.
Comparing LLM responses between survey question variants that use the phrasing 'not allowed' versus 'forbidden' to detect if the wording alters the outcome.
Reversing the order of multiple-choice options to detect primacy bias, determining if models exhibit a preference for options placed at the top of a list.
Evaluating shifts in LLM response distributions when a 'don't know' option is introduced to a question scale to see if models inappropriately distribute responses.
Measuring how LLM responses redistribute to weak agree/disagree options when a neutral middle option is added to or removed from a multiple-choice scale.
